title: Hema Malini Credits 'Hanuman Ji Ki Kripa' for 'Hanuman Ansh' Rs 150-Crore Run
excerpt: The veteran actor said she was "very happy" the Neem Karoli Baba devotional drama became a box-office phenomenon, and praised first-time producer Anupriya Nagar for backing it.
body:
• Veteran actor and MP Hema Malini said she was "very happy" that the devotional drama Hanuman Ansh has become a huge box office success, calling it "Hanuman ji ka kripa" — the grace of Lord Hanuman.
  • The film, written and directed by Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi and based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, opened on August 7 with just Rs. 10 lakh and has since crossed Rs. 150 crore net in India.
  • Malini also lauded first-time producer Anupriya Nagar for backing the spiritual film despite having no prior experience in filmmaking.
  • Hanuman Ansh is scheduled for an international release on September 11, 2026, taking the sleeper hit to overseas audiences.

Veteran actor and parliamentarian Hema Malini has weighed in on the most unlikely box-office story of 2026, saying she was "very happy" that the devotional drama Hanuman Ansh has become a huge commercial success. The film, based on the life and teachings of Neem Karoli Baba, opened on August 7 with a mere Rs. 10 lakh and has since stormed past Rs. 150 crore net at the Indian box office — a turnaround that has stunned the trade.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=omvSRCNdxHk

"Hanuman ji ka kripa hai," Malini said, describing the film's run as the grace of Lord Hanuman. She also reserved praise for producer Anupriya Nagar, lauding her for backing a spiritual film despite having no prior experience in filmmaking, according to reports of her remarks.

The remark that set the tone

Malini's comments, reported by Hindustan Times, framed the film's success not as a marketing triumph but as something closer to a blessing. The language matters in the context of the film itself: Hanuman Ansh is rooted in what its makers call "Bharat's timeless Sant Parampara," tracing the early life of Lakshmi Narayan in pre-Independence India and his spiritual journey across North India before emerging as Neem Karoli Baba — the saint revered by devotees as an incarnation of Lord Hanuman, known for his teachings of love, devotion and service.

https://x.com/ZoomTV/status/2097707970469810637

"Hanuman ji ka kripa hai."

— Hema Malini, actor and MP

The film's devotional core has drawn endorsements from across the public sphere. Actor and MP Preity Zinta said she was highly impressed and urged people not to miss it, while BJP national president Nitin Nabin said he wanted to watch it. Actor Tusshar Kapoor also spoke about the film, describing it as his first devotional project in decades.

A box-office turnaround for the record books

The numbers behind Hanuman Ansh read like a screenplay. The film opened on approximately 250 screens with Rs. 10 lakh on its first Friday, followed by Rs. 23 lakh on Saturday and Rs. 31 lakh on Sunday — a first weekend of just Rs. 64 lakh. Week one closed at Rs. 1.07 crore; week two took the cumulative total to only Rs. 1.57 crore.

Then came the reversal. From day 16 the film began climbing — Rs. 95 lakh on day 16, Rs. 2.58 crore on day 17 — and the fourth week changed everything: Rs. 6.68 crore on day 22, Rs. 9.97 crore on day 23 and Rs. 13 crore on day 24. By the end of week four the film had accumulated Rs. 74.81 crore, and on day 30 it added Rs. 16.85 crore to cross the Rs. 100 crore mark.

The fifth weekend alone brought in Rs. 44 crore, taking the total past Rs. 113 crore, and on day 34 the film crossed Rs. 150 crore net in India, with gross collections nearing Rs. 170 crore. It is the sixth release of 2026 to cross Rs. 100 crore — and by far the slowest to get there. Made on a reported budget of just Rs. 1.75–2 crore and distributed across India by Cinépolis India, which scaled the release from roughly 40 screens in week two to more than 2,000 at its peak, the film has become the year's genuine sleeper phenomenon.

Context: the team behind it

Hanuman Ansh was written, directed and produced by Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi, and features Shobhina W Satyaa, Vihaan S Hegde, Chandan Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil K Rastogi and Gulshan Pandey. Its producers include Ragini S, Namrata G Singh, Anupriya A Nagar and Chaturvedi himself.

The film's message — "love all, serve all, feed all and remember Ram," in the words of its makers — found its audience through word of mouth rather than opening-weekend spectacle. Its growth curve inverts the usual pattern: instead of front-loading its business, the film grew into a major theatrical success over several weeks, powered by repeat family audiences and devotional circuits.

The diaspora angle

For the diaspora, the next chapter is the most relevant one. After its extraordinary domestic run, Hanuman Ansh is scheduled for an international release on September 11, 2026 — bringing the Neem Karoli Baba story to overseas theatres just as the film's legend is peaking at home. Devotional cinema has a proven diaspora audience, from the US and UK to the Gulf, and exhibitors will be watching whether the word-of-mouth magic travels.

What's next

The film is still adding crores daily — day 33 brought Rs. 11 crore at nearly 48% occupancy — so its final tally remains open. The larger question for the industry is whether Hanuman Ansh is a one-off miracle or a template: a micro-budget devotional drama that outperformed films costing fifty times more. Either way, Hema Malini's verdict has entered the lore of the season — this one, she says, belongs to Hanuman ji.
